exam-06-q01.why_correct_en: British citizens and permanent residents are expected to respect and obey the law and to look after themselves and their families. Other responsibilities include respecting others' rights, treating people fairly and caring for the area and environment where they live.

exam-06-q02.why_correct_en: Iron Age peoples produced the first coins minted in Britain, from roughly the second century BC. Many were influenced by continental Celtic and Greek designs, while later issues carried the names of local rulers, providing evidence about societies with few written records.

exam-06-q03.why_correct_en: William the Conqueror began the Tower of London after the Norman Conquest, with the White Tower built from the 1070s. It projected royal power over London and later served as fortress, palace, prison, armoury, mint and home of the Crown Jewels.

exam-06-q04.why_correct_en: National parks are protected areas of countryside valued for landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage. They are not untouched reserves: people live and work in them, and park authorities balance conservation with public enjoyment and sustainable local communities.

exam-06-q05.why_correct_en: False. Northern Ireland has no established church. The Church of Ireland was disestablished in 1871; today Christianity includes several major denominations, especially Catholic, Presbyterian, Church of Ireland and Methodist traditions.

exam-06-q06.why_correct_en: Great Britain comprises England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom but not Great Britain; this is why the state's full name is the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

exam-06-q07.why_correct_en: Prime Minister's Questions is normally held every Wednesday when the Commons is sitting. For about 30 minutes the Prime Minister answers questions from MPs, including a sequence from the Leader of the Opposition, making it a prominent form of parliamentary scrutiny.

exam-06-q08.why_correct_en: Charles I was executed in 1649 after Parliament's victory in the Civil Wars. He was tried for high treason and beheaded outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall; England then became a republic before the monarchy was restored in 1660.

exam-06-q09.why_correct_en: William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564. He later worked in London as an actor, playwright and shareholder in the Lord Chamberlain's Men, but retired to Stratford and was buried in Holy Trinity Church there.

exam-06-q10.why_correct_en: Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson and Ellie Simmonds are celebrated British Paralympians. Grey-Thompson won 11 Paralympic wheelchair-racing gold medals; swimmer Simmonds won two golds at Beijing 2008 when she was only 13.

exam-06-q11.why_correct_en: English settlement on the eastern coast of North America began during Elizabeth I's reign, although the Roanoke colonies failed. The first permanent English settlement, Jamestown, was founded in 1607 under James I, so the question refers to the beginning of colonising attempts.

exam-06-q12.why_correct_en: False. Individual Electoral Registration was introduced across Great Britain, not only Scotland and Wales. Each eligible person registers themselves rather than one 'head of household' registering everyone; England, Scotland and Wales all use this individual system.

exam-06-q13.why_correct_en: The birth of Jesus Christ is celebrated on Christmas Day, 25 December. It is a major Christian festival and a UK bank holiday; Advent is the preparatory season before Christmas, while Boxing Day follows on 26 December.

exam-06-q14.why_correct_en: The Battle of Britain was primarily an aerial battle in summer and autumn 1940 between the RAF and Germany's Luftwaffe. Britain's radar and fighter-control network helped prevent Germany gaining air superiority, a prerequisite for a planned invasion.

exam-06-q15.why_correct_en: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales, on Swansea Bay. It grew through copper smelting and port trade during the Industrial Revolution and is near the Gower Peninsula, designated Britain's first Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.

exam-06-q16.why_correct_en: The Conservative Party and Liberal Democrats formed a coalition after the 2010 election produced a hung Parliament. David Cameron became Prime Minister and Nick Clegg Deputy Prime Minister; it was the first full UK coalition government since the Second World War.

exam-06-q17.why_correct_en: Henry VIII established royal supremacy over the Church of England after the Pope would not annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon. The 1534 Act of Supremacy recognised the king as supreme head, separating the English church from papal authority.

exam-06-q18.why_correct_en: The Black Death reached Britain in 1348. The plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, killed a huge share of the population; the resulting labour shortage increased many surviving workers' bargaining power and contributed to long-term social change.

exam-06-q19.why_correct_en: Haggis is a traditional Scottish dish made from sheep's offal mixed with oatmeal, onion and spices. It is strongly associated with Burns Night on 25 January, when Robert Burns's poem Address to a Haggis is often recited.

exam-06-q20.why_correct_en: Scotland's Justice of the Peace Courts deal with less serious criminal cases under summary procedure. A JP court cannot impose imprisonment and has lower sentencing powers than a sheriff court, illustrating Scotland's distinct legal system.

exam-06-q21.why_correct_en: The Domesday Book and Bayeux Tapestry both illuminate William I's England. Domesday recorded landholding and resources in 1086 for royal administration; the embroidery narrates the events leading to the 1066 Norman Conquest and Battle of Hastings.

exam-06-q22.why_correct_en: Irish Home Rule was delayed because the First World War began in 1914. The Home Rule Act passed that year but its operation was suspended; the Easter Rising, independence war and treaty then transformed the issue, leading to partition in 1921.

exam-06-q23.why_correct_en: The true statement is that Elizabeth I was a Protestant who sought a middle course between Catholic practice and more radical Protestant demands. The 1559 Religious Settlement restored royal supremacy and a Protestant prayer book while retaining some traditional forms.

exam-06-q24.why_correct_en: A National Insurance number application requires evidence of identity and, where relevant, permission to work in the UK. The number links a person's National Insurance contributions and tax records; it is not itself proof of identity or a right to work.
